subject: POC prep: success criteria, timeline, and credentials
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandra Torres <atorres@cloudvista.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC prep: success criteria, timeline, and credentials

Hi Alejandra — great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking us through your goals. Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed-upon POC plan and the immediate asks so we have a single reference. Please review and flag anything missing.

Summary of objectives (what success looks like for CloudVista):
- Latency: median per-response latency under 350ms for shortest prompts (<=128 tokens) and p95 under 900ms for evaluation traffic (simulated at 10rps).
- Cost proxy: token spend under $X (we'll convert to an estimate after we know average prompt lengths).
- Quality: precision on the 50-item prompt-eval set >= 86% (you said 80–90 target range).
- Integration: API-based inference + embedding lookups integrated into your staging app with SSO-controlled access.

Proposed timeline:
- Aug 4: Provision test credentials + SSO invite; engineering kickoff (30–60m).
- Aug 5–11: Run evaluation harness, collect metrics, and iterate on prompt templates.
- Aug 12: 1-hour checkpoint to review results and next steps for scale.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Grace (eng/product lead) for project coordination; Dev Patel (dev_patel) for credentialing and infra support.
- CloudVista: Alejandra (PM) for success criteria, and secops for SSO/IP gating.

Immediate asks for CloudVista (action items):
1) Provide the SSO IdP metadata or a SAML/OIDC connection point and the email of the admin we should invite.
2) Provide the outbound IPs you will allowlist so we can issue the scoped test key (or tell us if you prefer IPs on your side).
3) Confirm the evaluation window and any blackout periods.

Attachments: PoC-Scope-and-Success-Map-v1.pdf (high-level plan & metrics we discussed).

Next steps: Dev will follow up with exact credential format and a short-lived test API key plan. If that works, can we lock Aug 4, 10:00am PT for the kickoff?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alejandra Torres <atorres@cloudvista.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudVista Security <secops@cloudvista.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prep: success criteria, timeline, and credentials

Thanks Grace — this is perfect and matches our notes. A few quick clarifications: 

- Success criteria: the team is comfortable with the latency targets; for cost, we asked for a conservative estimate once you have sample token counts.
- Evaluation set: I'll send the 50-item prompt list and our expected answers by EOD today.
- SSO: Please invite our IdP admin Alejandra Torres (same email). We use Okta; secops is cc'd to provide the metadata.

On IP allowlisting — secops prefers to provide our allowed-list on our end. If you need to whitelist Redwood outbound IPs, please send the CIDR blocks and we will confirm.

We can do the kickoff Aug 4, 10:00am PT. Please send the calendar invite.

One ask from my side: for the POC, can Redwood provide a short-lived API token limited to inference-only with an expiry of 7 days? That will make it easier for our security review.

Thanks,
Alejandra
Product Manager, CloudVista
atorres@cloudvista.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alejandra Torres <atorres@cloudvista.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prep: success criteria, timeline, and credentials

Hi Alejandra — looping in technical details and the credentialing approach.

Credential plan (short-lived token + scoped access):
- We can issue a scoped API key with inference-only permissions, usage limits (tokens/min) and a 7-day TTL as requested.
- For integrations that require SSO, we'll send a SAML invite to the admin you indicate; the SSO account will map to a Redwood project role that enforces RBAC.

IP allowlist options (pick one):
A) You allowlist Redwood outbound CIDRs and we issue the test key (fastest).
B) Redwood issues a key restricted to your configured IPs (we still need at least one source IP for callbacks/health checks).

If you go with A, here are the outbound CIDRs to whitelist in your firewall: 34.197.120.0/24, 52.44.10.0/24, 3.218.90.0/24 (these are for our dedicated POC pool).

Sample curl (inference):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED-POC-TOKEN>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-7b","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":128}'

I'll attach a short instructions file with the token lifecycle and SSO steps.

Attachments: redwood-poc-credentials-instructions.txt (config + example responses).

I'll provision the test key once secops confirms the CIDRs or provides an alternate.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Perfect — appreciate the fast follow-up. Dev, please proceed with issuing a scoped, 7-day inference-only key bound to the two staging IPs secops provided and share the key-create template (JSON) in the morning. Alejandra — I'll send the calendar invite for Aug 4, 10:00am PT now.

Best,
